title: Understanding Mutual Fund Taxation: Equity vs Debt Gains
description: The taxation of gains from mutual funds in India depends significantly on whether they are equity-oriented or debt-oriented funds. Equity mutual funds held fo.

faq.q: What is an equity-oriented mutual fund for tax purposes?
faq.a: An equity-oriented mutual fund is one that invests at least 65% of its assets in Indian equities. This classification determines its eligibility for specific equity taxation rules, such as the ₹1 lakh LTCG exemption.

faq.q: Is indexation still available for debt mutual funds?
faq.a: No, for debt mutual fund units purchased on or after April 1, 2023, the benefit of indexation for long-term capital gains has been removed. All gains are now taxed at your income tax slab rate.

Hybrid funds are taxed based on their equity exposure. If they hold 65% or more in Indian equities, they are treated as equity funds. If they hold less than 65% in Indian equities, they are treated as debt funds for taxation purposes.

faq.q: What is the grandfathering rule for equity LTCG?
faq.a: The grandfathering rule protects gains made on equity mutual fund investments until January 31, 2018, from the new 10% LTCG tax. The cost of acquisition is adjusted to the NAV as of January 31, 2018, to calculate taxable gains.

faq.q: Are dividends from mutual funds tax-free?
faq.a: No, dividends distributed by mutual funds are fully taxable in the hands of the investor at their applicable income tax slab rate. Fund houses also deduct TDS if the dividend amount exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year.

faq.q: How are international mutual funds taxed?
faq.a: International mutual funds, which invest in foreign equities, are generally treated as debt funds for taxation purposes. For units purchased after April 1, 2023, all gains are taxed at your income tax slab rate.
